label: UTF-8
comments: For “encoding” formats, the extension given should have “.txt” appended to it when it’s not being used as an option for another format (e.g. HTML). Variants: unicode versions, BOM/no BOM, line ending variants (CR/LF/CRLF/the various others floating around), PUA extensions (variant:unicodePua type).

label: Internal: Classic Dc Array
comments: Array of classic (short) Dc ints, without a defined repreresentation - &[u32] in Rust; an in StageL

label: Dc Integer List
comments: ASCII text containing list of integers representing classic Dcs. Strictly, one space after every int, and no newlines. Loosely, with newlines or multiple spaces, or no end space.

label: Printable ASCII
comments: ASCII with no control characters. Variants: Line ending variants allowed for *reading*, but only CR/LF/CRLF, and all of them mean unambiguous CR+LF (=EOL), and should be interpreted as such on import and emitted as such on export, thus preserving line-endings by requiring non-CRLF to be stored using a higher-level protocol (e.g. base64ing the content and using this as an ASCII armor format only). How useful this format is is debateable.

label: ASCII
comments: 7-bit ASCII. Variants: Line ending variants

label: SEMS
comments: Space-separated list of ints representing classic Dcs, with comments. Comments are UTF-8. Strictly, one space after every int, valid UTF-8 comments only, and a final newline.

label: Unicode
comments: Array of ints representing Unicode characters. Might include things that aren’t valid unicode.

label: VT100
comments: Terminal format is an option for text files; when exporting would get the extension format: [terminal].[encoding].txt for example: vt100.utf8.txt

label: Character-mode terminal
comments: Variants: terminal, encoding

label: Character-mode teleprinter
comments: Variants: terminal, encoding. (A printer that can overstrike etc. would still be considered immutable; immutable refers to whether it can erase. Raster, postscript, etc. printers would use their respective formats rather than this one.)

label: Dc in Unicode
comments: unicodePua = extension to Unicode using the Private Use Areas

label: BaseNb family
comments: data = format that can hold generic binary data (or at least, generic sequences of bytes; not all formats support generic numbers of bits).

label: HTML fragment
comments: Variants: same as HTML

label: Text
comments: HTML and text both should default to UTF8 as the default encoding. Encodings fill a somewhat odd role since they are both encodings and formats (with the text format plus a given encoding being the same thing as that encoding by itself).

label: English
comments: Most formats have language variant types, for printing structured metadata where it’s not supported. Whether it should be printed by default is debateable.

label: English (US)
comments: Language variants aren’t handled as format variants of the languages they are variants of, since there aren’t tons of possible combinations (at least that are practical to support). Instead, the type is given as lv: followed by the language identifier of which they are a variant (without the lang_ prefix).

label: JavaScript
comments: Programming languages are both formats on their own account, and variants of other formats: for exporting to a text-based format, you could opt to have programmatic Dcs exported to a programming language or a natlang.

label: Semantic Dcs to text
comments: “transformation” types operate on documents stored as arrays of Dcs.

label: Color-coded HTML integer list
comments: HTML file containing color-coded Dc integer list

Comma-separated Dc list
comments: ASCII text containing list of integers representing new Dcs, separated by commas, with no newlines. Loosely, with optional newlines, or spaces after commas. A parser could reasonably delegate to handling it as DcAsciiList if there are Dcs separated only by spaces, though a file mixing commas and spaces without commas should be rejected.
